guided_journeys.tagline: Someone has swapped the greenhouse’s energy stores and structural materials.
guided_journeys.premise: The Carbohydrate Greenhouse opens to chaos. Sweet seedlings are in the wrong beds, storage jars are mixed with structural fibers, and a suspicious alpha/beta path keeps redirecting the vines.
guided_journeys.mission: Follow the sugar trail from single units to larger carbohydrates, recover the storage molecules, rebuild the structural walls, and discover how some animals gain access to cellulose with microbial help.
guided_journeys.finale: At the Cellulose Fiber Barn, the missing feed labels are recovered and the symbiotic microbes return to work. Suki closes the greenhouse ledger. One sugar route now connects small building blocks, storage, structure, linkage, and digestion.

scenes.title: Mono-Sugar Seedling
scenes.story_open: Suki hands you the first seedling: a small carbohydrate unit built mainly from carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.
scenes.story_close: A sugar seedling grows toward the Sucrose Trellis, where single units begin pairing into larger carbohydrates.

story_beats.story: Three element tokens feeding one carbohydrate seedling. Carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen tokens feed the seedling while one carbonyl marker and several hydroxyl markers attach to the carbohydrate model.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Carbohydrate composition.
story_beats.science: PPT describes carbohydrates as containing carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen, with carbonyl and multiple hydroxyl groups.
story_beats.hint: three element tokens feeding one carbohydrate seedling

story_beats.story: One sugar sack resting alone in a cradle. Only one simple sugar unit sits in the cradle; a connector points from that one unit toward a future polysaccharide chain.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Monosaccharide.
story_beats.science: Monosaccharides are simple sugars and are the monomers for polysaccharides.
story_beats.hint: one MONO sugar SACK

story_beats.story: A formula card repeating CH₂O units beneath an exception warning. The card repeats CH₂O as n increases, but a permanent warning prevents the pattern from becoming an exceptionless rule.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Monosaccharide CH2O pattern.
story_beats.science: Many monosaccharides have molecular formulas that are generally multiples of CH2O, making (CH2O)n a useful pattern rather than an exceptionless rule.
story_beats.hint: a formula card repeating CH₂O units beneath an exception warning

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? Monosaccharides are simple sugars and are the monomers for polysaccharides.

scenes.title: Sucrose Trellis
scenes.story_open: The trellis is covered with glucose tags and paired sugar units. Two monosaccharides can become a disaccharide such as sucrose.
scenes.story_close: The paired sugars feed a vine that refuses to stop growing, pulling you into the Polysaccharide Vine.

story_beats.story: A GLUE-coated sugar cube feeding a cellular-respiration fuel meter. The sugar cube feeds the nutrient/fuel meter that leads into cellular respiration.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Glucose.
story_beats.science: PPT identifies glucose as a common monosaccharide used as a nutrient/fuel and in cellular respiration.
story_beats.hint: a GLUE-coated sugar cube feeding the fuel meter

story_beats.story: One monosaccharide unit entering two labeled destination lanes. One monosaccharide moves toward an amino-acid building route while another lane feeds di- and polysaccharide assembly.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Monosaccharides as building blocks.
story_beats.science: PPT states that monosaccharides can serve as building blocks for amino acids or as monomers for di- and polysaccharides.
story_beats.hint: one monosaccharide unit entering two labeled destination lanes

story_beats.story: Two sugar sacks held by one covalent clasp. Exactly two monosaccharides are held together by one covalent connection.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Disaccharide.
story_beats.science: A disaccharide consists of two monosaccharides joined by a covalent bond.
story_beats.hint: two DI sugar sacks joined by one clasp

story_beats.story: SUE CROW tying one glucose cube to one fruit-marked fructose cube. Sue Crow joins glucose and fructose into one pair, then carries that pair into a plant transport tube.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Sucrose.
story_beats.science: PPT identifies sucrose as glucose + fructose and as a carbohydrate transport form in plants.
story_beats.hint: SUE CROW tying a glucose cube to a FRUIT sugar cube

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? PPT identifies glucose as a common monosaccharide used as a nutrient/fuel and in cellular respiration.

scenes.title: Polysaccharide Vine
scenes.story_open: The vine keeps growing. Repeated sugar units extend into long polysaccharide structures.
scenes.story_close: The long chains split into two corridors: one leads to the Storage Pantry Alcove and the other will eventually become structural material.

story_beats.story: A POLY vine made of many sugar sacks, with one linear arm and one branched arm. Many sugar monomers become one carbohydrate polymer; one section remains linear while another branches.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Polysaccharide.
story_beats.science: Polysaccharides are carbohydrate polymers composed of many sugar monomers; the CED notes that complex carbohydrate polymers may be linear or branched.
story_beats.hint: a POLY many-sugar-sack vine

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? Polysaccharides are carbohydrate polymers composed of many sugar monomers; the CED notes that complex carbohydrate polymers may be linear or branched.

scenes.title: Storage Pantry Alcove
scenes.story_open: Two storage doors open. Plants stock starch here; animals store glycogen in a more highly branched form.
scenes.story_close: A burst storage jar sends sugar chains across the hall and into the Structural Wall Alcove, where similar units serve a completely different role.

story_beats.story: A plant pantry shelf storing bundled glucose units. The plant shelf stores excess glucose as a glucose polymer.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Starch.
story_beats.science: Starch is a glucose polymer used by plants for storage of excess glucose.
story_beats.hint: a plant grain-storage shelf packed with glucose bundles

story_beats.story: A GLYCO sugar GENIE guarding glucose bundles inside liver and muscle compartments. The genie locks glucose-polymer stores into an animal liver compartment and an animal muscle compartment.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Glycogen.
story_beats.science: Glycogen is a glucose polymer used by animals for storage, including in liver and muscle cells.
story_beats.hint: a GLYCO sugar GENIE guarding liver-and-muscle storage

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? Starch is a glucose polymer used by plants for storage of excess glucose.

scenes.title: Structural Wall Alcove
scenes.story_open: The greenhouse walls are built from cellulose, while a tougher chitin panel appears in other biological structures.
scenes.story_close: A loose cellulose panel swings open and reveals the Glycosidic Archway holding sugar units together.

story_beats.story: Sugar fibers woven directly into a plant CELL wall. The sugar polymer fibers become part of the wall itself, supporting the plant cell structurally.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Cellulose.
story_beats.science: Cellulose is a structural polysaccharide forming plant cell walls.
story_beats.hint: a plant CELL wall woven from strong sugar fibers

story_beats.story: A KITTEN fitted inside a crab-like arthropod shell. The kitten remains inside the rigid arthropod exoskeleton so the sound cue stays bound to structural function.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Chitin.
story_beats.science: PPT identifies chitin as a structural polysaccharide in arthropod exoskeletons.
story_beats.hint: a KITTEN wearing an arthropod shell

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? Cellulose is a structural polysaccharide forming plant cell walls.

scenes.title: Glycosidic Archway
scenes.story_open: A sugar arch locks units together with glycosidic linkages. Nearby, alpha and beta glucose orientations send polymers toward different architectures.
scenes.story_close: The arch forks at an alpha/beta marker, forcing you onto the Alpha/Beta Path to see how a small orientation difference changes the polymer.

story_beats.story: A GLYCO bridge covalently joining two monosaccharide rings. The bridge forms a covalent connection between two monosaccharides; a small 1→4 case-study marker can appear without requiring exact polymer reproduction.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Glycosidic linkage.
story_beats.science: A glycosidic linkage is a covalent bond joining monosaccharides. In the packet's starch/cellulose case study, 1→4 linkages connect carbon 1 of one glucose to carbon 4 of the next.
story_beats.hint: a GLYCO sugar bridge joining two sugar units

story_beats.story: Greek α and β markers beside glucose rings with opposite carbon-1 hydroxyl orientations. The carbon-1 hydroxyl orientation is shown one way in the α model and the opposite way in the β model.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Alpha and beta glucose.
story_beats.science: Alpha and beta glucose differ in the orientation of the hydroxyl group attached to carbon 1 when glucose forms a ring. Campbell uses this distinction to explain different glycosidic linkages in starch and cellulose. This exact structural detail is enrichment because the current CED excludes specific carbohydrate-polymer molecular structures from AP Exam scope.
story_beats.hint: Greek α and β beside two glucose-ring orientation models

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? A glycosidic linkage is a covalent bond joining monosaccharides. In the packet's starch/cellulose case study, 1→4 linkages connect carbon 1 of one glucose to carbon 4 of the next.

scenes.title: Alpha/Beta Path
scenes.story_open: Two paths look almost identical at the first glucose unit, then diverge into storage-friendly starch and straight cellulose fibers.
scenes.story_close: The cellulose path ends at a barn full of plant fiber that the animals cannot digest alone. The final clue is inside the Cellulose Fiber Barn.

story_beats.story: An α track curling/branching toward storage while a β track runs straight into aligned chains. The α-linked route produces a starch-like helical/branch-capable storage form, while the β-linked route produces straight unbranched cellulose chains that align.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Starch versus cellulose structure.
story_beats.science: Starch contains alpha-glucose linkages that produce storage structures that may be helical and, in amylopectin, branched. Cellulose contains beta-glucose linkages; its chains are straight and unbranched and can align into strong hydrogen-bonded microfibrils. The exact polymer structures are teacher-enrichment, not current AP-required structural recall.
story_beats.hint: an α track curling/branching toward storage while a β track runs straight into aligned chains

story_beats.story: Parallel cellulose chains held side by side by dashed hydrogen-bond crosslinks. Hydrogen bonds form between neighboring parallel cellulose chains, grouping them into strong microfibrils.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Cellulose fiber organization.
story_beats.science: Parallel cellulose chains can form hydrogen bonds with one another, grouping the chains into strong microfibrils that contribute mechanical strength to plant cell walls.
story_beats.hint: parallel cellulose chains held side by side by dashed hydrogen-bond crosslinks

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: Explain this locked scientific relationship in ordinary scientific language: Starch contains alpha-glucose linkages that produce storage structures that may be helical and, in amylopectin, branched. Cellulose contains beta-glucose linkages; its chains are straight and unbranched and can align into strong hydrogen-bonded microfibrils. The exact polymer structures are teacher-enrichment, not current AP-required structural recall.

scenes.title: Cellulose Fiber Barn
scenes.story_open: At the barn, cellulose-rich feed reaches animals that cannot digest it alone. Symbiotic microbes do the chemical work their hosts cannot.

story_beats.story: Cellulose fibers stopping at an animal-enzyme gate while mutualistic microbes open a fermentation route. The animal’s own enzyme gate cannot hydrolyze cellulose, but mutualistic microorganisms ferment the cellulose in a specialized digestive compartment.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Cellulose digestion by symbiotic microbes.
story_beats.science: Animals do not produce cellulase enzymes that hydrolyze cellulose. Cellulose-digesting herbivores obtain access to cellulose energy through mutualistic microorganisms that carry out fermentation in specialized digestive compartments.
story_beats.hint: cellulose fibers stopping at an animal-enzyme gate while mutualistic microbes open a fermentation route

story_beats.story: A cow taking a four-room stomach route while a horse is diverted to a separate enlarged-cecum hindgut route. The cow moves rumen → reticulum → omasum → abomasum while the horse bypasses that route and enters an enlarged-cecum/large-intestine fermentation path.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Ruminant stomach compartments.
story_beats.science: In a cow, a ruminant, the four stomach chambers are the rumen, reticulum, omasum, and abomasum. Mutualistic microorganisms digest cellulose in the rumen/reticulum; water is removed in the omasum; the abomasum carries out digestion with the cow's enzymes. Horses are not ruminants; they are hindgut fermenters that house cellulose-digesting microorganisms mainly in an enlarged cecum and large intestine.
story_beats.hint: a four-room cow route, with the horse diverted to a separate hindgut path

guided_journeys.tagline: A famous client’s protein has unfolded minutes before delivery. Rebuild it before the shipment leaves.
guided_journeys.premise: The Protein Factory is in emergency mode. A finished protein has lost its shape, and the client is waiting. Milo gives you the raw amino-acid pieces and tells you there is no shortcut: sequence, chemistry, folding, and assembly all have to work.
guided_journeys.mission: Rebuild the protein from amino acids, connect the chain correctly, follow the folding levels, and protect the finished structure from the denaturation furnace.
guided_journeys.finale: The rebuilt protein reaches the Function Showroom, folds correctly, and switches on its function lamp. Milo seals the package just before the loading door closes. The entire protein story now runs from sequence to structure to function.

scenes.title: Protein Entrance
scenes.story_open: Milo rolls in a damaged protein. The machine only works when a polypeptide reaches the right three-dimensional shape, and the rebuild starts with amino acids.
scenes.story_close: Milo places the damaged protein on a cart and sends you to the Amino-Acid Workbench to rebuild it from the smallest useful pieces.

story_beats.story: A folded-chain machine that powers a function lamp only after it takes a stable 3D shape. An unfolded chain passes through the folding gate; only the organized three-dimensional form switches on the function lamp.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Protein.
story_beats.science: A protein consists of one or more polypeptide chains folded into a three-dimensional shape; protein shape determines function.
story_beats.hint: a folded polypeptide becomes a functional machine

story_beats.story: C, H, O, and N badges lock onto the common amino-acid frame while a sulfur badge appears only in a selected side-bin. C, H, O, and N badges stay on the common amino-acid framework; sulfur appears only on selected side chains and never receives an EVERY PROTEIN stamp.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Protein elements.
story_beats.science: Protein amino acids necessarily contain carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen in their common backbone. Sulfur occurs in some amino acids, including cysteine and methionine, so sulfur is present in some proteins but is not an invariant element of every protein.
story_beats.hint: C, H, O, and N badges lock onto the common amino-acid frame while a sulfur badge appears only in a selected side-bin

story_beats.story: A rack with exactly twenty distinct amino-acid slots. Exactly twenty standard amino-acid cards click into twenty separate rack slots used for proteins.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Twenty amino acids.
story_beats.science: PPT states that there are 20 different amino acids in the standard set used in proteins.
story_beats.hint: a rack with exactly twenty distinct amino-acid slots

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? A protein consists of one or more polypeptide chains folded into a three-dimensional shape; protein shape determines function.

scenes.title: Amino-Acid Workbench
scenes.story_open: One amino-acid frame sits under a lamp: central carbon, hydrogen, amino group, carboxyl group, and one variable side chain.
scenes.story_close: The variable side chain on the amino-acid frame keeps changing, so Milo drops the pieces into the R-Group Sorting Tank.

story_beats.story: A central hub holding H, a carboxyl arm, an amine arm, and one changeable R backpack. The central carbon holds four attachments: hydrogen, carboxyl group, amine group, and the variable R group; the model stays conceptual rather than becoming an AP exact-structure drawing task.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Amino acid.
story_beats.science: Amino acids are protein building blocks. The CED specifies a central carbon, hydrogen, carboxyl group, amine group, and variable R group.
story_beats.hint: a central-carbon figure carries an AMINO group and a CARBOXYL group plus H and an R backpack

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? Amino acids are protein building blocks. The CED specifies a central carbon, hydrogen, carboxyl group, amine group, and variable R group.

scenes.title: R-Group Sorting Tank
scenes.story_open: Different R-group backpacks enter a water tank. Nonpolar ones avoid water; polar and charged ones behave differently, changing how the chain will fold.
scenes.story_close: Once the side-chain behaviors are sorted, the amino acids reach the Peptide-Tie Station and begin joining into a chain.

story_beats.story: One detachable backpack marked R that changes what happens when it is swapped. The same amino-acid frame receives different R backpacks, and each swap changes the side chain’s chemical behavior.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is R group.
story_beats.science: Each amino acid has a variable side chain (R group) whose chemical properties differ among amino acids.
story_beats.hint: a detachable backpack marked R changes each amino acid's behavior

story_beats.story: An oily R backpack that turns away from surrounding water. The nonpolar backpack avoids the water-facing side of the tank and moves into the water-avoiding lane.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Nonpolar R group.
story_beats.science: R groups may be nonpolar/hydrophobic.
story_beats.hint: an oily R backpack that turns away from surrounding water

story_beats.story: An R backpack that reaches toward surrounding water droplets. The polar backpack turns toward the water-facing side of the tank and remains in the hydrophilic lane.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Polar R group.
story_beats.science: R groups may be polar/hydrophilic.
story_beats.hint: an R backpack that reaches toward surrounding water droplets

story_beats.story: An R backpack carrying either a plus or minus magnet while remaining water-facing. A charged R backpack stays water-facing; the acidic lane carries a minus sign and the basic lane carries a plus sign at cellular pH.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Ionic R group.
story_beats.science: Charged amino-acid side chains are generally hydrophilic. Acidic side chains are usually negatively charged at cellular pH, while basic side chains are usually positively charged.
story_beats.hint: an R backpack carrying either a plus or minus magnet while remaining water-facing

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? Each amino acid has a variable side chain (R group) whose chemical properties differ among amino acids.

scenes.title: Peptide-Tie Station
scenes.story_open: The assembly clamp joins amino acids with peptide bonds, releasing water during dehydration as the polypeptide grows.
scenes.story_close: The growing chain leaves the clamp and lands on the N/C Conveyor, which forces you to track its two different ends.

story_beats.story: A bright PEP-TIE clamp joining one carboxyl side to the next amino/amine side. The clamp joins the carboxyl group of one amino acid directly to the amino/amine group of the next.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Peptide bond.
story_beats.science: A peptide bond is a covalent bond linking amino acids; it forms between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino/amine group of the next.
story_beats.hint: a bright PEP-TIE ties the carboxyl side of one amino acid to the amino side of the next

story_beats.story: A joining clamp that sends one water droplet down the drain as the amino acids connect. As the amino acids are joined, a water droplet leaves the station; the joining direction is never confused with hydrolysis.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Peptide-bond dehydration.
story_beats.science: PPT represents peptide-bond formation as a dehydration reaction.
story_beats.hint: a joining clamp that sends one water droplet down the drain as the amino acids connect

story_beats.story: A long chain spool built from many amino-acid units connected by repeated PEP-TIES. The spool grows as many amino acids are linked together by repeated peptide bonds into one continuous chain.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Polypeptide.
story_beats.science: A polypeptide is a chain of many amino acids linked by peptide bonds.
story_beats.hint: a long chain with many PEP-TIES

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? A peptide bond is a covalent bond linking amino acids; it forms between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino/amine group of the next.

scenes.title: N/C Conveyor
scenes.story_open: The new chain rides a conveyor with two chemically distinct ends. Direction matters from the N-terminus to the C-terminus.
scenes.story_close: The directional chain feeds directly into the Sequence Folding Machine, where its order begins controlling what shape can form.

story_beats.story: One chain conveyor with an N-marked entrance and a chemically different C-marked exit. The same chain is traced from its N-terminus end to its chemically distinct C-terminus end; the two end labels never exchange positions.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Polypeptide directionality.
story_beats.science: PPT states that each polypeptide has directionality with a chemically distinct N-terminus and C-terminus.
story_beats.hint: one chain conveyor with an N-marked entrance and a chemically different C-marked exit

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: Explain this locked scientific relationship in ordinary scientific language: PPT states that each polypeptide has directionality with a chemically distinct N-terminus and C-terminus.

scenes.title: Sequence Folding Machine
scenes.story_open: Milo feeds the sequence into the folding machine. Change the amino-acid order and the pattern of R-group interactions can change the final shape.
scenes.story_close: The first stable fold lights a delivery ticket and sends the molecule into the Function Showroom to prove that shape has consequences.

story_beats.story: A fixed-order bead strip entering a folding machine and producing a corresponding overall shape. Changing the bead order changes the primary sequence entering the machine, so the resulting folding pathway and overall shape can change.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Sequence determines shape.
story_beats.science: Specific amino-acid sequence determines primary structure and contributes to overall protein shape.
story_beats.hint: a fixed-order bead strip entering a folding machine and producing a corresponding overall shape

story_beats.story: R side-chain contact points pulling one chain into a particular fold and switching a function indicator. As R-group contact points interact, the chain changes its folding pattern; the resulting structure changes the function indicator.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled R-group interactions determine folding.
story_beats.science: PPT and CED connect R-group interactions with protein structure and function.
story_beats.hint: R side-chain contact points pulling one chain into a particular fold and switching a function indicator

story_beats.story: A gene instruction strip selecting one ordered series of amino-acid beads. The instruction strip controls the order in which amino-acid beads appear on the polypeptide sequence rail.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Genes determine amino-acid sequence.
story_beats.science: PPT prompts students to connect gene information with the unique amino-acid sequence of a polypeptide.
story_beats.hint: a gene instruction strip selecting one ordered series of amino-acid beads

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: Explain this locked scientific relationship in ordinary scientific language: Specific amino-acid sequence determines primary structure and contributes to overall protein shape.

scenes.title: Function Showroom
scenes.story_open: Finished proteins enter a showroom filled with jobs: structure, transport, signaling, defense, movement, catalysis, and more.
scenes.story_close: The showroom elevator refuses to certify the protein until you inspect every structural level, so Milo sends you into the Four-Level Elevator.

story_beats.story: One folded-machine display rotating through catalyst, shield, signal, support beam, transport cart, and storage locker roles. One folded protein machine rotates through six labeled roles: enzymatic catalysis, defense, signaling, structural support, transport, and storage; a small hormone placard says SOME HORMONES.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Protein functions.
story_beats.science: Proteins perform diverse functions, including enzymatic catalysis, defense, signaling, structural support, transport, and storage; some hormones are proteins.
story_beats.hint: one folded-machine display rotating through catalyst, shield, signal, support beam, transport cart, and storage locker roles

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: Explain this locked scientific relationship in ordinary scientific language: Proteins perform diverse functions, including enzymatic catalysis, defense, signaling, structural support, transport, and storage; some hormones are proteins.

scenes.title: Four-Level Elevator
scenes.story_open: The elevator begins with primary structure and rises through increasingly complex levels. Every level contributes to the final functional form.
scenes.story_close: The elevator stops first at the Secondary Folding Room, where local backbone interactions create recognizable patterns.

story_beats.story: Floor 1 displaying only one linear ordered amino-acid chain. The elevator stops at Floor 1, where only the ordered amino-acid sequence is visible before any higher-level folding is shown.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Primary structure.
story_beats.science: Primary structure is the linear amino-acid sequence; PPT states that it is determined via genes and influences higher levels.
story_beats.hint: Floor 1 shows only the linear amino-acid sequence

story_beats.story: One function console wired to Floors 1, 2, 3, and 4. Wires from all four structural floors converge on the same function console, so changing structural organization at any level can matter for function.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled All levels determine function.
story_beats.science: All four levels of protein structure contribute to protein function.
story_beats.hint: one function console wired to Floors 1, 2, 3, and 4

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? Primary structure is the linear amino-acid sequence; PPT states that it is determined via genes and influences higher levels.

scenes.title: Secondary Folding Room
scenes.story_open: Local regions of the chain fold into alpha helices and beta-pleated sheets through backbone hydrogen bonding.
scenes.story_close: Those local folds are only part of the job. The chain is pulled into the Tertiary Interaction Chamber for whole-chain folding.

story_beats.story: Local stretches of the backbone being pinned into coils and sheets by hydrogen bonds. Hydrogen-bond pins act on the polypeptide backbone and stabilize local coils and folds without yet representing the complete 3D fold of one chain.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Secondary structure.
story_beats.science: Secondary structure consists of local coils and folds of the polypeptide backbone produced by hydrogen bonding, including alpha helices and beta-pleated sheets.
story_beats.hint: Floor 2 folds local backbone segments into a helix or sheet

story_beats.story: A large α-shaped guide coiling one backbone segment into a spring while hydrogen-bond pins hold the coil. The α guide coils the local backbone segment and hydrogen-bond pins stabilize the resulting spring-like structure.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Alpha helix.
story_beats.science: Alpha helix is a secondary structure stabilized by hydrogen bonding within the polypeptide backbone.
story_beats.hint: a giant α/A winds into a spring-like helix

story_beats.story: A β marker laying neighboring backbone stretches across one pleated platform while hydrogen-bond pins connect them. Neighboring stretches of polypeptide backbone align across the pleated platform and are stabilized by hydrogen bonds; a SAME CHAIN POSSIBLE sign prevents the separate-chain misconception.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Beta-pleated sheet.
story_beats.science: A beta-pleated sheet is a secondary structure stabilized by hydrogen bonds between atoms of the polypeptide backbone in neighboring stretches of chain; separate polypeptide chains are not required.
story_beats.hint: a giant β/B lies on a pleated bedsheet

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? Secondary structure consists of local coils and folds of the polypeptide backbone produced by hydrogen bonding, including alpha helices and beta-pleated sheets.

scenes.title: Tertiary Interaction Chamber
scenes.story_open: The whole chain folds further as side chains interact through hydrophobic effects, hydrogen bonding, ionic interactions, and sometimes disulfide bridges.
scenes.story_close: When one folded chain is not enough, a loading door opens to the Quaternary Assembly Bay and multiple subunits arrive.

story_beats.story: One entire polypeptide folding into one overall three-dimensional shape inside a single-chain cradle. The cradle accepts exactly one polypeptide and folds the whole chain into its overall 3D shape through side-chain interactions.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Tertiary structure.
story_beats.science: Tertiary structure is the overall three-dimensional folding of one polypeptide produced by side-chain interactions.
story_beats.hint: Floor 3 folds one polypeptide into its overall 3D shape

story_beats.story: Four required interaction stations plus one clearly optional close-contact station acting on side chains. The side-chain panel cycles through hydrogen-bond contacts, a hydrophobic huddle, plus/minus ionic attraction, and an S—S disulfide connection; a separate Campbell-only close-contact indicator represents van der Waals interactions.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Tertiary interactions.
story_beats.science: Tertiary protein structure is stabilized by side-chain interactions including hydrophobic interactions, van der Waals interactions, hydrogen bonds, ionic interactions, and covalent disulfide bridges. The AP CED explicitly requires hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, ionic interactions, and disulfide bridges.
story_beats.hint: four required interaction stations plus one clearly optional close-contact station acting on side chains

story_beats.story: Two sulfur ends snapping together into one bright S—S bridge clamp. Two sulfur atoms from two cysteine side chains form one covalent S—S connection that helps stabilize tertiary structure.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Disulfide bridge.
story_beats.science: A disulfide bridge is a covalent bond formed between the sulfur atoms of two cysteine side chains and can help stabilize protein tertiary structure.
story_beats.hint: two sulfur atoms clasp into a bright S—S bridge

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? Tertiary structure is the overall three-dimensional folding of one polypeptide produced by side-chain interactions.

scenes.title: Quaternary Assembly Bay
scenes.story_open: Multiple polypeptide subunits arrive at the assembly bay and combine into one functional protein when quaternary structure is required.
scenes.story_close: The assembled protein passes inspection, but Milo deliberately places an unfinished chain beside it at Raw Chain Inspection.

story_beats.story: Several folded subunits docking around a QUARTET sound-sign while a large MULTIPLE, NOT FOUR counter stays lit. Multiple folded polypeptide subunits dock into one protein assembly; the count display stays at “multiple” while the quartet sign serves only as the name cue.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Quaternary structure.
story_beats.science: Quaternary structure arises from association/interactions among multiple polypeptide chains and occurs only in proteins with multiple subunits.
story_beats.hint: a QUARTET of polypeptide subunits assembles into one protein

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? Quaternary structure arises from association/interactions among multiple polypeptide chains and occurs only in proteins with multiple subunits.

scenes.title: Raw Chain Inspection
scenes.story_open: Milo stops the belt. A polypeptide chain is not automatically the same thing as a fully folded, functional protein.
scenes.story_close: To see why environment matters, the raw and folded chains are lowered into the Soluble-Protein Water Tank.

story_beats.story: A raw amino-acid chain on one side of an inspection gate and a folded working assembly on the other. The inspector labels the linear peptide-bonded chain as one category and only stamps the folded, organized one-or-more-chain assembly as the functional category.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Polypeptide versus protein.
story_beats.science: A polypeptide is a linear chain of amino acids linked by peptide bonds. A functional protein consists of one or more polypeptide chains folded and organized into a specific three-dimensional structure.
story_beats.hint: a raw amino-acid chain waits beside a folded working machine

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? A polypeptide is a linear chain of amino acids linked by peptide bonds. A functional protein consists of one or more polypeptide chains folded and organized into a specific three-dimensional structure.

scenes.title: Soluble-Protein Water Tank
scenes.story_open: A soluble protein enters water. Hydrophilic regions tend to face outward while hydrophobic regions are often buried away from the aqueous environment.
scenes.story_close: A temperature alarm suddenly sounds. The protein is rushed toward the Denaturation Furnace for the final stress test.

story_beats.story: Hydrophobic side chains moving inward while polar and charged side chains face the surrounding water. Inside the water tank, nonpolar/hydrophobic side chains tend to bury in the protein interior while polar and charged side chains tend to face outward; a membrane-protein warning prevents overgeneralization.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled R-group orientation in aqueous environments.
story_beats.science: For soluble proteins in an aqueous environment, nonpolar/hydrophobic side chains often become buried in the protein interior, while polar and charged side chains are often exposed to water. This pattern is context-dependent and should not be overgeneralized to membrane proteins.
story_beats.hint: hydrophobic side chains moving inward while polar and charged side chains face the surrounding water

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: Explain this locked scientific relationship in ordinary scientific language: For soluble proteins in an aqueous environment, nonpolar/hydrophobic side chains often become buried in the protein interior, while polar and charged side chains are often exposed to water. This pattern is context-dependent and should not be overgeneralized to membrane proteins.

scenes.title: Denaturation Furnace
scenes.story_open: The furnace temperature spikes. Higher-order interactions fail, the protein loses shape, and function can disappear even though peptide bonds are not being treated as ordinary heat-broken links.

story_beats.story: Heat or extreme conditions unfolding a working protein while an unbroken peptide-chain rail remains continuous. The stabilizing interactions are disrupted, the native 3D shape collapses, and function is lost while the peptide backbone remains intact under ordinary denaturing conditions.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Denaturation.
story_beats.science: Protein denaturation is loss of a protein's native three-dimensional structure, often causing loss of function, when conditions disrupt the interactions stabilizing the protein. In the packet's DNA context, 'denaturation' refers to separation of the two DNA strands when noncovalent base-pairing interactions are disrupted; it does not mean the phosphodiester backbone is hydrolyzed.
story_beats.hint: heat/pH turns a neatly folded protein into a disordered 'de-natured' chain

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? Protein denaturation is loss of a protein's native three-dimensional structure, often causing loss of function, when conditions disrupt the interactions stabilizing the protein. In the packet's DNA context, 'denaturation' refers to separation of the two DNA strands when noncovalent base-pairing interactions are disrupted; it does not mean the phosphodiester backbone is hydrolyzed.

guided_journeys.learner_rule: Listen or read. Imagine the scene. Pause only at occasional Quick Recall cards. If recall is weak, ask for the scene or a hint; otherwise keep moving.
guided_journeys.narrative_design: One palace premise + one mission + one recurring guide + causal route + science-bearing actions + restrained distinctiveness. No decorative event may introduce a new scientific claim.

guided_journeys.tagline: A damaged archive has scattered the pieces of a genetic message.
guided_journeys.premise: A storm has damaged the Nucleic Acid Archive. Pages of a genetic manuscript have come apart into sugars, bases, phosphates, and paired strands. The archive will not reopen until the message is reconstructed in the correct direction.
guided_journeys.mission: Rebuild the manuscript from nucleotide parts, restore strand direction and pairing, and carry the recovered sequence safely through the melting room.
guided_journeys.finale: The repaired double helix locks into the archive case and the sequence catalog comes back online. Nia turns the key. You can now retrace how components become strands, how strands pair, and how sequence carries information.

scenes.title: DNA/RNA Front Desk
scenes.story_open: Nia opens two damaged archive cases labeled DNA and RNA. Both are nucleic acids, but their usual structures and components are not identical.
scenes.story_close: One torn archive page slides under the Nucleotide Pass Counter, where its molecular pieces must be checked before reconstruction can begin.

story_beats.story: A long chain of nucleotide tiles feeding into a locked hereditary-information vault. A long nucleotide chain enters the vault, and the vault stores, transmits, or helps express hereditary information.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Nucleic acid.
story_beats.science: Nucleic acids are nucleotide polymers involved in storing, transmitting, and expressing hereditary information.
story_beats.hint: an information archive stores long nucleotide chains

story_beats.story: Two contrasting information scrolls, one with a de-oxygenated sugar and T marker and one with a ribose sugar and U marker. The two scrolls enter the same nucleic-acid archive but remain side-by-side for later sugar, base, strand, and pairing distinctions.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is DNA and RNA.
story_beats.science: The two forms emphasized are deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ribonucleic acid (RNA).
story_beats.hint: two archive scrolls, one DNA and one RNA, are compared side-by-side

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term or target matches this locked course definition? Nucleic acids are nucleotide polymers involved in storing, transmitting, and expressing hereditary information.

scenes.title: Nucleotide Pass Counter
scenes.story_open: At the counter, a complete entry pass requires a nitrogenous base, a five-carbon sugar, and phosphate. A side lane admits base plus sugar without phosphate.
scenes.story_close: The recovered bases are still unsorted. Nia carries them into the Ring Reading Room and lays them out by ring structure.

story_beats.story: An entry pass assembled from a base card, a five-sided sugar token, and a phosphate tag. The counter refuses the pass until all three components are present together.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Nucleotide.
story_beats.science: For AP Biology, a nucleotide is described as a nitrogenous base, a five-carbon sugar, and a phosphate group. Free nucleotide precursors may carry more than one phosphate, while an incorporated polynucleotide unit contributes one phosphate to the sugar-phosphate backbone.
story_beats.hint: a three-piece entry pass has BASE + SUGAR + PHOSPHATE

story_beats.term: Backbone phosphate in an incorporated nucleotide
story_beats.story: A free precursor tray beside a stamped sugar-phosphate backbone rail. A free precursor may arrive carrying more than one phosphate, but after incorporation one phosphate occupies the sugar-phosphate backbone connection for that nucleotide unit.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Backbone phosphate in an incorporated nucleotide.
story_beats.science: Within a polynucleotide, adjacent nucleotide units are connected through phosphate groups in the sugar-phosphate backbone; the incorporated nucleotide contributes one backbone phosphate.
story_beats.hint: a free precursor tray beside a stamped sugar-phosphate backbone rail

story_beats.story: A base card and sugar token standing SIDE-by-side while phosphate waits outside the lane. The base and sugar pass together through the side lane, but the phosphate tag is stopped outside.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Nucleoside.
story_beats.science: PPT defines the nucleoside portion as base + sugar without phosphate.
story_beats.hint: BASE and SUGAR stand SIDE-by-side with no phosphate

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term or target matches this locked course definition? For AP Biology, a nucleotide is described as a nitrogenous base, a five-carbon sugar, and a phosphate group. Free nucleotide precursors may carry more than one phosphate, while an incorporated polynucleotide unit contributes one phosphate to the sugar-phosphate backbone.

scenes.title: Ring Reading Room
scenes.story_open: The base cards are sorted by ring architecture: purines have two rings; pyrimidines have one.
scenes.story_close: The sorted base cards are useless without the correct sugars, so the archive cart moves into the DNA/RNA Sugar Gallery.

story_beats.story: A PYRAMID DINES at a table with one ring and seats labeled C, T, and U. C, T, and U all sit at the single-ring table while the two-ring table remains separate.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Pyrimidine.
story_beats.science: PPT classifies cytosine, thymine, and uracil as pyrimidines with a single ring in its structural depiction.
story_beats.hint: a PYRAMID DINES at a ONE-RING table

story_beats.story: A PURRING cat wearing two fused rings beside A and G cards. A and G attach to the two-ring cat while the C/T/U one-ring table remains separate.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Purine.
story_beats.science: PPT classifies adenine and guanine as purines with two fused rings in its structural depiction.
story_beats.hint: a PURRING cat wears TWO rings

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term or target matches this locked course definition? PPT classifies cytosine, thymine, and uracil as pyrimidines with a single ring in its structural depiction.

scenes.title: DNA/RNA Sugar Gallery
scenes.story_open: Four exhibits separate DNA from RNA through sugar and base differences: deoxyribose versus ribose, thymine versus uracil.
scenes.story_close: With DNA and RNA components separated, the pieces reach the Backbone Bridge and are connected into directional strands.

story_beats.story: THYME herb resting on a large T card at the deoxy-sugar display. The T card stays with the DNA display and later pairs with A at the base-pair table.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Thymine.
story_beats.science: Thymine is a nitrogenous base used in DNA.
story_beats.hint: THYME herb sits on a large T card inside the DNA archive

story_beats.story: A seal saying 'YOU’RE A SEAL' while holding a U card at the ribose display. The U card stays with the RNA display and later pairs with A at the base-pair table.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Uracil.
story_beats.science: Uracil is a nitrogenous base used in RNA.
story_beats.hint: a seal shouts 'YOU'RE A SEAL!' while holding a U card on an RNA scroll

story_beats.story: A sugar RIB cage with one oxygen symbol crossed out on the DNA shelf. The crossed-oxygen sugar locks onto the DNA shelf while the uncrossed ribose cue remains on the RNA shelf.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Deoxyribose.
story_beats.science: DNA contains the five-carbon sugar deoxyribose.
story_beats.hint: a RIB cage sugar has one oxygen symbol crossed out

story_beats.story: An intact sugar RIB cage on the RNA shelf. The intact sugar cue locks onto the RNA shelf while the deoxy cue remains on the DNA shelf.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Ribose.
story_beats.science: RNA contains the five-carbon sugar ribose.
story_beats.hint: a RIB cage made of sugar sits on the RNA scroll

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term or target matches this locked course definition? Thymine is a nitrogenous base used in DNA.

scenes.title: Backbone Bridge
scenes.story_open: The damaged manuscript has two different strand ends. One carries a 5′ phosphate; the other a 3′ hydroxyl, and phosphodiester linkages connect neighboring nucleotides.
scenes.story_close: The strand is incomplete. A blinking arrow points toward the 3′ Growth Desk, where only one end can accept the next nucleotide.

story_beats.story: A glowing 5′ flag carrying a phosphate marker at one end of a sugar-phosphate bridge. The 5′ phosphate flag remains fixed at one end while the opposite end is reserved for the 3′ hydroxyl dock.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled 5′ phosphate end.
story_beats.science: Nucleic acids have a 5′ phosphate end; PPT places phosphate at the 5′ carbon of the sugar.
story_beats.hint: a glowing 5′ flag carrying a phosphate marker at one end of a sugar-phosphate bridge

story_beats.story: A glowing 3′-OH docking light at the opposite end of the bridge. The 3′-OH light remains opposite the 5′ phosphate flag and becomes the site emphasized for strand extension.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled 3′ hydroxyl end.
story_beats.science: Nucleic acids have a 3′ hydroxyl end.
story_beats.hint: a glowing 3′-OH docking light at the opposite end of the bridge

story_beats.story: One phosphate bridge gripping two ESTHER handles attached to neighboring sugars. The phosphate clamp joins adjacent nucleotides through neighboring sugars to form the covalent sugar-phosphate backbone connection.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Phosphodiester linkage.
story_beats.science: PPT identifies phosphodiester linkage as the covalent linkage connecting adjacent nucleotides through the sugar-phosphate backbone.
story_beats.hint: a PHOSPHATE bridge grips TWO 'ESTHER' twins, one on each neighboring sugar

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term or target matches this locked course definition? PPT identifies phosphodiester linkage as the covalent linkage connecting adjacent nucleotides through the sugar-phosphate backbone.

scenes.title: 3′ Growth Desk
scenes.story_open: New nucleotides can be added only at the growing 3′ end, so the strand is synthesized in the 5′→3′ direction.
scenes.story_close: As the strand lengthens, the order of bases begins forming a message. Nia carries it straight to the Sequence Catalog.

story_beats.story: A clerk adding each incoming nucleotide only at the glowing 3′-OH socket. Every incoming nucleotide is directed to the 3′ loading socket; the 5′ end is never used as the depicted addition site.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled 3′-end nucleotide addition.
story_beats.science: During nucleic-acid synthesis, nucleotides are added to the 3′ end of the growing strand.
story_beats.hint: a clerk adding each incoming nucleotide only at the glowing 3′-OH socket

story_beats.story: A one-way route arrow running from a 5′ marker toward the active 3′ growth desk. The strand is read as having chemically distinct 5′ and 3′ ends, with the growth direction represented toward the 3′ end.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled 5′→3′ directionality.
story_beats.science: Nucleic acid strands have directionality defined by 5′ and 3′ ends.
story_beats.hint: a one-way route arrow running from a 5′ marker toward the active 3′ growth desk

story_beats.story: An incoming nucleotide repeatedly docking at the same glowing 3′-OH bay. The tray rejects any attempt to dock the incoming nucleotide at the 5′ end and accepts it only at the 3′ growth site.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Nucleotide addition to 3′ end.
story_beats.science: During nucleic-acid polymerization, a new nucleotide is added to the 3′ end of the growing strand.
story_beats.hint: a new nucleotide always docks at the glowing 3′-OH loading bay

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term or target matches this locked course definition? During nucleic-acid polymerization, a new nucleotide is added to the 3′ end of the growing strand.

scenes.title: Sequence Catalog
scenes.story_open: Nia restores the catalog by placing nucleotides in order. The sequence itself stores biological information.
scenes.story_close: The catalog can read the message, but it cannot protect it until a complementary strand is rebuilt on the Antiparallel Spiral Staircase.

story_beats.story: A scanner reading the order of nucleotide-letter tiles along a scroll and sending that order toward a protein instruction board. Rearranging the letter order changes the encoded information sent forward; the scanner follows sequence order, not the mere presence of the letters.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Nucleotide sequence encodes information.
story_beats.science: Biological information is encoded in the linear nucleotide sequence; PPT connects gene base sequence to amino-acid sequence and protein structure.
story_beats.hint: a scanner reading the order of nucleotide-letter tiles along a scroll and sending that order toward a protein instruction board

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: Explain this locked scientific relationship in ordinary scientific language: Biological information is encoded in the linear nucleotide sequence; PPT connects gene base sequence to amino-acid sequence and protein structure.

scenes.title: Antiparallel Spiral Staircase
scenes.story_open: Two strands twist into a double helix while running in opposite orientations. The staircase only closes correctly when the strands are antiparallel.
scenes.story_close: The two opposite-running strands twist together and descend to the Base-Pair Reading Table for pairing inspection.

story_beats.story: Two polynucleotide rails twisting together into one spiral staircase. The two rails twist around the same axis while remaining distinct strands.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled DNA double helix.
story_beats.science: DNA consists of two antiparallel polynucleotide strands twisted into a double helix.
story_beats.hint: two polynucleotide rails twisting together into one spiral staircase

story_beats.story: Two lines of ANTS walking on parallel helical rails in opposite directions. One rail is oriented 5′→3′ while the partner rail runs in the opposite orientation.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Antiparallel.
story_beats.science: DNA strands are antiparallel and run in opposite 5′ to 3′ orientations.

scenes.title: Base-Pair Reading Table
scenes.story_open: At the reading table, complementary bases pair predictably: A with T and C with G in DNA, while RNA commonly uses U in place of T and can fold back on itself.
scenes.story_close: The paired manuscript passes every base check, then enters the DNA Melting Room for one final test of strand stability.

story_beats.story: An A card clasping a T card across the DNA page with dashed hydrogen-bond marks. The A and T cards pair across the DNA page through hydrogen-bond representation while U remains on the RNA page.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled A–T base pairing.
story_beats.science: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine via hydrogen bonds.
story_beats.hint: an A card clasping a T card across the DNA page with dashed hydrogen-bond marks

story_beats.story: A C card clasping a G card across the base-pair table. C and G remain paired together in the DNA representation and are reused as a valid complementary pair in RNA.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled C–G base pairing.
story_beats.science: In DNA, cytosine pairs with guanine via hydrogen bonds.
story_beats.hint: a C card clasping a G card across the base-pair table

story_beats.story: One RNA ribbon folding back on itself so complementary regions can meet. The single ribbon bends back and forms paired regions without becoming a second separate full-length partner strand.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled RNA is typically single stranded.
story_beats.science: RNA is typically single stranded and can fold through complementary base pairing within the same RNA molecule.
story_beats.hint: one RNA ribbon folding back on itself so complementary regions can meet

story_beats.story: An A card clasping the U card on the RNA page. A pairs with U on the RNA page while the DNA page keeps A paired with T.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled A–U base pairing.
story_beats.science: In RNA, adenine pairs with uracil.
story_beats.hint: an A card clasping the U card on the RNA page

story_beats.story: A folded RNA ribbon bringing a C card against a G card. When the single RNA strand folds, a C and G region meet and pair within the folded molecule.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled RNA C–G base pairing.
story_beats.science: Cytosine can pair with guanine by hydrogen bonding in RNA, just as C–G pairing occurs in DNA.
story_beats.hint: a folded RNA ribbon bringing a C card against a G card

scenes.title: DNA Melting Room
scenes.story_open: Heat begins separating the paired strands by disrupting noncovalent stabilizing interactions. GC-rich regions generally require higher temperatures under comparable conditions.

story_beats.story: An A–T pair displaying two dashed connections beside a G–C pair displaying three. The counters display two and three while a warning light blocks the inference that bond count alone determines melting behavior.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Base-pair hydrogen-bond count comparison.
story_beats.science: In DNA, an A–T base pair forms two hydrogen bonds and a G–C base pair forms three. The difference can contribute to stability, but hydrogen-bond count should not be encoded as the sole determinant of DNA duplex thermal stability.
story_beats.hint: A–T uses TWO dashed handshakes while G–C uses THREE

story_beats.story: Heat opening the paired DNA zipper while both sugar-phosphate rails remain continuous. Heat separates the complementary strands, but neither covalent sugar-phosphate backbone is cut.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is DNA denaturation.
story_beats.science: Heating can separate complementary DNA strands by disrupting the noncovalent interactions that stabilize the double helix; the covalent sugar-phosphate backbones remain intact in ordinary thermal denaturation.
story_beats.hint: heat opens the DNA zipper between the two strands without cutting either sugar-phosphate rail

story_beats.story: Two equal-length DNA sections heating side-by-side while the GC-richer section remains paired to a higher temperature and a context panel shows stacking, length, and ionic conditions. Under the same comparison conditions, the GC-richer section requires a higher temperature to separate, while the context panel prevents a hydrogen-bond-only explanation.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled GC content and thermal stability.
story_beats.science: DNA regions with higher G–C content generally melt at higher temperatures than equivalently sized lower-GC regions under comparable conditions. Do not explain this only by counting hydrogen bonds: DNA thermal stability also depends on nearest-neighbor sequence/stacking interactions, strand length, ionic conditions, and other thermodynamic factors.
story_beats.hint: two equal-length DNA sections heating side-by-side while the GC-richer section remains paired to a higher temperature and a context panel shows stacking, length, and ionic conditions

guided_journeys.tagline: A living-cell exhibit is losing its membrane as the temperature swings.
guided_journeys.premise: The Lipid Membrane Wing houses a living-cell exhibit. Tonight its membrane is failing: lipid pieces are scattered, fatty-acid tails are packing incorrectly, and the temperature control keeps swinging.
guided_journeys.mission: Rebuild the lipid components, assemble a phospholipid bilayer, identify the steroid framework, and use cholesterol to stabilize the membrane across temperature changes.
guided_journeys.finale: The final cholesterol molecules settle into the membrane and the thermostat stops oscillating. Lena watches the cell recover. The wing now tells one connected story about hydrophobic molecules, fat structure, bilayers, steroids, and membrane fluidity.

scenes.title: Lipid Lobby
scenes.story_open: Lena sweeps up oily molecules that avoid mixing with water. The wing contains several lipid types, and one of them will become the cell’s membrane.
scenes.story_close: One oily molecule rolls away from a water spill and lands beneath the Glycerol Hook Rack, where the first lipid components are waiting.

story_beats.story: An oil-rich molecular guest reaches the water fountain and beads away from it. The oil-rich guest avoids mixing with the fountain water, while a two-sided phospholipid marker shows that some lipids also contain a hydrophilic region.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Lipid.
story_beats.science: Lipids are a diverse group of molecules with substantial hydrophobic character because of their hydrocarbon-rich regions. Many are largely nonpolar, while phospholipids are amphipathic, with a hydrophilic head and hydrophobic tails. Lipids do not include true polymers.
story_beats.hint: an oil-rich molecular guest beads away from water

story_beats.story: Three doors marked by a fat droplet, a membrane-forming head-and-tail icon, and a four-ring frame, with a cholesterol card displayed inside the ring section. The directory sorts course examples into fats, phospholipids, and steroids; the cholesterol card remains within lipid examples and is later identified as a steroid.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Major lipid types.
story_beats.science: PPT emphasizes fats, phospholipids, and steroids; the CED also includes cholesterol within lipid examples.
story_beats.hint: three doors marked by a fat droplet, a membrane-forming head-and-tail icon, and a four-ring frame, with a cholesterol card displayed inside the ring section

scenes.title: Glycerol Hook Rack
scenes.story_open: A glycerol scaffold waits beside long fatty-acid tails. In a fat, three fatty acids join one glycerol.
scenes.story_close: Three fatty-acid tails swing from the rack and are carried to the Ester-Linkage Bench to be connected covalently.

story_beats.story: One central rack holds exactly three long fatty-acid tails. Three fatty-acid tails attach to one glycerol scaffold as a single fat assembly.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Fat composition.
story_beats.science: PPT describes fats as glycerol joined to three fatty acids.
story_beats.hint: one central rack holds exactly three long fatty-acid tails

story_beats.story: A GLITTER-ROLL spindle carries several alcohol-like OH hooks. The spindle presents hydroxyl-group hooks and then serves as the central scaffold to which fatty acids can attach in a fat.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Glycerol.
story_beats.science: PPT describes glycerol as an alcohol containing hydroxyl groups.
story_beats.hint: GLITTER-ROLL with hydroxyl hooks

story_beats.story: A long oily carbon-chain tail ends at one acidic carboxyl head. The long hydrocarbon region stretches across the tray while the carboxyl group stays fixed at one end, ready to join the glycerol scaffold.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Fatty acid.
story_beats.science: PPT describes fatty acids as long carbon chains with a carboxyl group at one end.
story_beats.hint: long oily carbon tail with one acidic carboxyl head

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? PPT describes glycerol as an alcohol containing hydroxyl groups.

scenes.title: Ester-Linkage Bench
scenes.story_open: An ester-linkage clamp connects glycerol and fatty acids during dehydration.
scenes.story_close: The finished lipid model rolls onto the Fatty-Acid Tail Runway, where straight and kinked tails pack very differently.

story_beats.story: ESTHER closes a covalent clasp between the glycerol scaffold and a fatty-acid tail as a water droplet leaves. A dehydration event removes the equivalent of water while the covalent clasp forms between glycerol and a fatty acid.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Ester linkage.
story_beats.science: In a fat, fatty acids are covalently joined to glycerol by ester linkages formed through dehydration reactions. Exact lipid molecular structures are teacher-supporting material, not AP-required structural memorization.
story_beats.hint: ESTHER closes a covalent clasp

scenes.title: Fatty-Acid Tail Runway
scenes.story_open: Straight saturated tails line one lane. Unsaturated tails carry C=C double bonds that create kinks, reduce tight packing, and increase room-temperature liquidity as unsaturation rises.
scenes.story_close: The runway ends at a storage door. The fat molecules disappear into the Fat Storage Vault, revealing why organisms keep them.

story_beats.story: A straight fatty-acid tail has only single carbon-carbon bonds and is filled with hydrogen markers. Because no carbon-carbon double bond interrupts the chain, the tail remains straight in the simplified course representation.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Saturated fatty acid.
story_beats.science: Saturated fatty acids contain only single bonds between carbon atoms; PPT describes them as having no C=C double bonds and more hydrogen.
story_beats.hint: straight hydrogen-full tail with no C=C

story_beats.story: A neighboring fatty-acid tail contains a C=C hinge and bends at the hinge. At least one carbon-carbon double bond interrupts the chain and produces the characteristic kink represented in the course scene.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Unsaturated fatty acid.
story_beats.science: Unsaturated fatty acids contain at least one C=C double bond.
story_beats.hint: C=C hinge creates a kinked tail

story_beats.story: One C=C hinge forces the tail to bend at that location. As soon as the C=C hinge locks in place, the previously straight runway tail bends.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Double-bond kink.
story_beats.science: A carbon-carbon double bond in an unsaturated fatty acid causes the carbon chain to kink.
story_beats.hint: one C=C hinge forces the tail to bend at that location

story_beats.story: A counter adds C=C hinges one by one and the unsaturation meter rises with each added hinge. Each added double-bond marker raises the unsaturation meter.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Unsaturation increases with double bonds.
story_beats.science: More double bonds in a fatty-acid tail mean greater unsaturation.
story_beats.hint: a counter adds C=C hinges one by one and the unsaturation meter rises with each added hinge

story_beats.story: Tails with more C=C hinges pack less tightly and the lipid sample flows more easily at room temperature. As double-bond hinges accumulate, tight packing is reduced in the representation and the room-temperature sample becomes more liquid.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Unsaturation and liquidity.
story_beats.science: Greater lipid unsaturation is associated with greater liquidity at room temperature.
story_beats.hint: tails with more C=C hinges pack less tightly and the lipid sample flows more easily at room temperature

scenes.title: Fat Storage Vault
scenes.story_open: The vault is packed for long-term energy storage, while padded stations also represent cushioning and thermal insulation.
scenes.story_close: A membrane alarm interrupts the tour. Lena pulls out phospholipids and rushes you to the Phospholipid Pool Wall.

story_beats.story: A dense long-term energy vault sits beside a soft organ cushion and a subcutaneous insulating layer. Stored fat supplies a long-term energy reserve, adipose padding cushions organs, and subcutaneous fat reduces heat loss; a small cell-support marker retains the CED wording.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Fat functions.
story_beats.science: The major function of fats is long-term energy storage; adipose tissue also cushions organs and subcutaneous fat can provide thermal insulation. The current CED additionally frames fats as supporting cellular function.
story_beats.hint: a dense long-term energy vault sits beside a soft organ cushion and a subcutaneous insulating layer

scenes.title: Phospholipid Pool Wall
scenes.story_open: Phospholipids arrive with hydrophilic heads and hydrophobic tails. In water they self-organize into a bilayer with tails protected inside.
scenes.story_close: The bilayer stabilizes, but a rigid four-ring molecule is still unidentified. The next clue waits in the Steroid Ring Gallery.

story_beats.story: One glycerol scaffold holds two fatty-acid tails and a phosphate-containing head region. The head region remains on one side of the glycerol scaffold while exactly two fatty-acid tails extend from the other side.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Phospholipid.
story_beats.science: PPT describes a phospholipid as glycerol attached to two fatty acids and a phosphate-containing head region.
story_beats.hint: PHOSPHATE-headed membrane lipid with two tails

story_beats.story: The phospholipid head faces the surrounding water while its two oily tails turn away from the water. The head remains exposed to water and the tails orient away from water toward the protected interior.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Hydrophilic head and hydrophobic tails.
story_beats.science: PPT describes the phospholipid head as hydrophilic and fatty-acid tails as hydrophobic.
story_beats.hint: the phospholipid head faces the surrounding water while its two oily tails turn away from the water

story_beats.story: Many head-and-tail molecules arrange into two opposing rows with heads facing water on both sides and tails meeting in the middle. The molecules self-organize so hydrophilic heads face aqueous environments and hydrophobic tails cluster together in the interior, forming a double layer.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Phospholipid bilayer.
story_beats.science: Phospholipids assemble into bilayers in water and form lipid bilayers of plasma and cell membranes.
story_beats.hint: many head-and-tail molecules arrange into two opposing rows with heads facing water on both sides and tails meeting in the middle

scenes.checkpoint_prompt: What exact scientific term matches this locked course definition? PPT describes a phospholipid as glycerol attached to two fatty acids and a phosphate-containing head region.

scenes.title: Steroid Ring Gallery
scenes.story_open: Rigid four-ring frameworks fill the gallery. Testosterone is one steroid example, and some steroids function as hormones.
scenes.story_close: One steroid card is marked cholesterol and points toward the temperature controls at the Cholesterol Thermostat Gate.

story_beats.story: A rigid frame is built from four fused carbon rings, with interchangeable side-group tags clipped around the frame. The four rings stay fixed while the attached-group tags change from one steroid example to another.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Steroid.
story_beats.science: PPT identifies steroids by a four-fused-ring framework and states that attached groups distinguish steroid types.
story_beats.hint: four fused carbon-ring frame

story_beats.story: A TEST paper strikes a TONE bell mounted inside one four-ring steroid frame. The test paper hits the tone bell only inside a steroid frame, marking this molecule as one example rather than the definition of the whole steroid class.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Testosterone.
story_beats.science: PPT gives testosterone as an example of a steroid.
story_beats.hint: TEST paper strikes a TONE bell inside the steroid frame

story_beats.story: Only some four-ring frames enter a control panel with growth, development, metabolism, and homeostasis dials. Selected steroid molecules adjust the four process dials while other steroid frames, including the cholesterol display, remain outside the hormone-only lane.
story_beats.reveal: Keep the relationship labeled Steroid hormone functions.
story_beats.science: Steroids are lipids characterized by four fused carbon rings. Some steroids function as hormones that regulate processes such as growth, development, metabolism, and homeostasis; not every steroid is a hormone.
story_beats.hint: only some four-ring frames enter a control panel with growth, development, metabolism, and homeostasis dials

scenes.title: Cholesterol Thermostat Gate
scenes.story_open: Cholesterol wedges among phospholipids. At high temperature it restrains movement; at low temperature it interferes with tight packing, buffering membrane fluidity.

story_beats.story: A COAL-colored ESTHER ROLL wedges among animal-membrane phospholipids beside a thermostat. At higher temperature the wedge restrains phospholipid movement; at lower temperature it interferes with tight tail packing, buffering membrane properties across temperature changes.
story_beats.reveal: The exact name to attach to that image is Cholesterol.
story_beats.science: Cholesterol is a steroid and common component of animal cell membranes. It acts as a membrane-fluidity buffer, restraining phospholipid movement at higher temperatures and hindering tight packing at lower temperatures, thereby helping maintain membrane properties across temperature changes.
story_beats.hint: COAL-colored ESTHER ROLL at a membrane thermostat
